decisionsTitle: A link replaced by a newer email says so — and every page that waits for an email points at Spam (amending §13.2's generic response and the spent-link decision)
decisionsSection:
**What happened.** An Administrator's resend — or the participant's own «Retrimite linkul» — queues the message again, and the outbox mints its link when it sends it (`notifications/render.ts`): `issueActionToken` invalidates the previous live link of the same purpose and scope and writes the new one, so two emails never carry two working links (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 5). A person who then pressed the *older* email landed on «Acest link nu mai este valabil. Îți putem trimite unul nou, pe aceeași adresă de email.» — the very words a guessed or mistyped address gets — and read it as "something broke". **The owner, 2026-10-01, during the Mailgun incident, after resending links to participants:** «când retrimit, primul link devine invalid? Userul trebuie să știe asta când îl deschide! Și trebuie să le spunem clar să verifice în spam».

**Why it was generic.** §202 gave a spent link (`ALREADY_USED`) a page that says where the registration stands, and kept `INVALIDATED` generic on purpose: `invalidated_at` held two facts in one column — superseded by a newer link (innocent, common) and revoked for cause (a decision to stop a link working) — and a page that coached its holder toward a fresh link would have treated both the same. The strict reading won "until the column can say which happened" (`domain/link-status.ts`).

**Decision.**

1. *The database tells the two apart.* `email_action_tokens.superseded_by_token_id uuid null references email_action_tokens(id) on delete set null` (migration `0117`, expand only: a column, its foreign key and the partial index). `issueActionToken` sets it in the same transaction, right after the insert, on exactly the rows its own UPDATE invalidated (by id, from `RETURNING`): two statements rather than one, so the reference never points at a row not yet written. Nothing else sets it; an invalidation from anywhere else is a revocation and leaves it null. `REGISTER_ANOTHER_PERSON` is never superseded (§420), so it never carries one. When the newer row is swept by retention (§322) the pointer goes null and the older row reads as revoked — generic, the strict reading, long past anybody's inbox. The column has a partial index on the non-null pointers (`email_action_tokens_superseded_by_idx`): the `set null` action runs as an UPDATE on it for every deleted row (retention, erasure cascades), which would otherwise scan a table that grows with every email sent (§327, §549). The foreign key was kept: the partial unique indexes ignore an invalidated row, so it did not collide with them.
2. *The evaluation names it.* `evaluateActionToken` returns `SUPERSEDED` (code `TOKEN_INVALID`) for an invalidated row that carries the pointer and `INVALIDATED` for the rest. The order is unchanged: purpose first (a link replayed at another endpoint stays indistinguishable from an unknown one), then superseded/revoked, used, expired. `readSupersededActionTokenScope` — the sibling of `readSpentActionTokenScope`, read-only, re-evaluating the row itself — gives a page the scope and one instant: when the newest token of the same purpose and scope was created, which is when its email was rendered. Never the newer token's id, hash or secret.
3. *The page says it.* For a superseded link of every purpose a newer link can replace — confirm address, declaration, waiting-list offer, manage, the public list's switch and «Înscrierile mele» (`MANAGE_PROFILE`) — the token page shows, in an `info` box in place of the generic warning, «Acest link a fost înlocuit. Ți-am trimis un email mai nou, cu un link valabil (trimis marți, 29 sept. 2026, la 10:00). Deschide cel mai recent email de la noi — dacă nu-l găsești, caută în Spam și în Promoții.» / "This link has been replaced. We sent you a newer email with a working link (sent …). Open the latest email from us — if you cannot find it, check Spam and Promotions." Two keys (`replaced`, `replacedAt`) chosen in code, the time on Romania's clock, the latest email's rather than the one the column names (after two resends the person is told to open the latest). The resend button stays under it, narrowed to the event as the spent page's is; «Înscrierile mele» keeps «Cere un link nou». The argument is §202's for `ALREADY_USED`, and it is structural: only an exact match on `token_hash` — SHA-256 of 32 random bytes — reaches the row, so whoever reached it holds the secret from that email, and "a newer email has the working link" tells them nothing the email in their hand did not, except which email to open. It reports no state.
4. *What stays generic, and why.* An unknown token has nothing to report; a link opened at another endpoint must stay indistinguishable from it; an expired link's only next step is the resend path the generic page already carries; a link revoked for cause must not coach its holder toward a fresh one. No code path revokes today — the column keeps the two facts apart for the day one does. `AGENTS.md` §13.2 now says both exceptions in one sentence.

**Spam, visibly.** Every page that tells somebody to wait for an email now shows one `info` box, the same words everywhere (`Registrations.spamHint.body`): «Nu a venit în câteva minute? Caută în Spam și în Promoții și mută-ne în Inbox, ca să primești și următoarele.» / "Nothing after a few minutes? Look in Spam and Promotions and move us to your inbox so the next ones arrive." — on the screen after the registration form (in place of the grey «Nu a venit? Uită-te și în Spam.»), under the sentence of the registration's resend form and of «Înscrierile mele»'s once sent, and under the newsletter's «Verifică-ți căsuța de email» and its unsubscribe-link answer. Those sentences lost their trailing «Verifică inclusiv folderul de spam» / «Nu îl găsești? Uită-te și în dosarul Spam.», which the box now says once. The replaced-link sentence names Spam itself and gets no second box. The short screen after a first form (§536) carries it too, under the bold «Emailul … pleacă» line and above the offer of another person: it is the screen most registrants see, since every non-member form ends there, not only a family's.

**Accepted:** the replaced-link sentence says the newer email has «un link valabil» without looking at the newest token: if that link was already used, expired or its registration cancelled since, the person opens the newer email and meets the spent or expired page, which says so and offers the resend. Checking would add a second read to a page that exists to be cheap, for a case that ends one click later on a truthful page.

**Nothing else moves.** Which links are invalidated and when, the purposes, the resend's limits and the throttle are as they were; every page reads with a GET in read-only transactions and changes nothing.

**Tests.** Unit: `tests/unit/tokens/action-token-state.test.ts` (SUPERSEDED only with the pointer, INVALIDATED without it, PURPOSE_MISMATCH still first, superseded before expired), `tests/unit/tokens/spent-link-status.test.ts` (`mayReportReplaced` opens for SUPERSEDED on every purpose but the family link, and for nothing else), `tests/unit/registrations/spam-hint.test.ts` (the box on the screen after the form, on its short variant after a first form, on both resend forms once sent and on the newsletter's two answers, in both languages). Integration on PGlite: `tests/integration/tokens/action-tokens.test.ts` (the pointer set on exactly the invalidated rows, profile tokens too, never on a used row or a family link; the reader's answers; a swept newer row reads as revoked) and `tests/integration/tokens/replaced-link-page.test.ts` (through the real Administrator resend and the real renderer: the earlier link's row points at the newer one; its confirmation page says «înlocuit» with the newer email's time in Romanian and English and keeps the resend path, and two GETs change no token; a revoked link, an unknown token and the replaced link opened at the declaration endpoint get the generic page; a replaced «Înscrierile mele» link says it too). e2e: `tests/e2e/registration-link-status.spec.ts` gains one test (a second link minted, the first opened: the box names a newer email) — compiled, not run.

*Rejected:* keeping the older link alive until the newer one is used — two working links in two emails, which BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 5 forbids; a sentence for every invalidated link — a revoked link would coach its holder toward a resend, undoing the revocation; the Spam hint only in the email — the person who cannot find the email never reads it.
changelogLine: - **An older link says a newer email replaced it** — after a resend, pressing the earlier email no longer lands on a generic «invalid» page; it says a newer email with a working link was sent and to look in Spam and Promotions; every page that waits for an email now says the same in a visible box. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given an action link invalidated because a newer link of the same purpose was issued, when it is opened, then the page says a newer email with a working link was sent (and when), tells the person to open the latest email and to check Spam and Promotions, and keeps the resend path; a link revoked for cause, an unknown token and a link opened at another endpoint still get the one generic response (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a submitted registration, when the screen after the form renders — and given the resend form or «Înscrierile mele»'s request form once sent — then the page shows a visible notice to look in Spam and Promotions and to move the club's emails to the inbox, the same words in Romanian and English on each (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: an older link says a newer email replaced it; Spam named on every waiting page
